ABSTRACT: Much attention has been focused on the catalytic
asymmetric creation of single chiral centers or two adjacent
stereocenters. However, the asymmetric construction of two
nonadjacent stereocenters is of significant importance but is
challenging because of the lack of remote chiral induction models.
Herein, based on a C�C bond relay strategy, we report a
synergistic Pd/Cu-catalyzed 1,5-double chiral induction model. All
four stereoisomers of the target products bearing 1,5-nonadjacent
stereocenters involving both allenyl axial and central chirality could
be obtained divergently by simply changing the combination of two
chiral catalysts with different configurations. Control experiments
and DFT calculations reveal a novel mechanism involving 1,5-
oxidative addition, contra-thermodynamic η
3
-allyl palladium shift, and conjugate nucleophilic substitution, which play crucial roles in
the control of reactivity, regio-, enantio-, and diastereoselectivity. It is expected that this C�C bond relay strategy may provide a
general protocol for the asymmetric synthesis of structural motifs bearing two distant stereocenters.
■
INTRODUCTION
Asymmetric catalysis is one of the most efficient protocols for
creating optically active compounds, which is of fundamental
importance in life science, medicinal chemistry, and materials
science.
1
A large number of synthetic approaches have been
developed to achieve the asymmetric construction of single
stereocenters and the simultaneous construction of two
adjacent stereocenters (Figure 1). However, very limited
reports have been disclosed on the one-step synthesis of
structural motifs bearing nonadjacent stereocenters.
2−5
It is
expected that the challenge will increase dramatically as the
distance between two stereogenic centers increases due to the
lack of reliable chiral induction models for both chiral entities.
To date, no example of the asymmetric catalytic construction
of 1,5-nonadjacent or more remote stereocenters has been
reported. Over the past decade, the synergistic catalysis
strategy has been proven to be a powerful synthetic tool to
asymmetrically access structural motifs bearing two stereo-
centers in a single step, such as two adjacent,

Allene chemistry has become an important branch in organic

10

catalytic asymmetric synthesis of chiral allenes.
11,12

construction of structural motifs bearing two distant stereo-
centers and could change the manner in which chemists think
about designing and building chiral molecules.

CONCLUSIONS
We have developed a protocol for 1,5-double chiral induction
based on a C�C bond relay strategy via a synergistic Pd/Cu
catalytic system, which was successfully applied to the
asymmetric construction of 1,5-nonadjacent stereocenters
bearing allenyl axial chirality and central chirality in a single
operation. A wide range of axial chiral allenes bearing a remote
stereocenter were readily synthesized in an enantio- and
diastereodivergent manner under mild reaction conditions.
Based on the control experiments and DFT calculations, a
reasonable mechanism with three key elementary reactions for
this 1,5-double chiral induction model involving 1,5-oxidative
addition, a contra-thermodynamic η
3
-allyl palladium shift, and
conjugate nucleophilic substitution has been proposed,
demonstrating the importance of the C�C bond relay
strategy for the reactivity and enantio- and diastereoselectivity
of the reaction. This strategy may provide a general avenue for
the asymmetric synthesis of chiral molecules bearing remote
nonadjacent stereocenters.
